paths.description: Homepage: discovery, search, navigation, consent, global performance/security and main content archetype.
Popular-content listing archetype, representing rankings and index pages.
Sample story/detail archetype, representing user-generated reading pages.
Primary creation form and anonymous editing/account-assistance journey.
Unknown-route recovery state for HTTP/runtime resilience.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark-theme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark/reduced-motion probe matched dark mode but body colors remained the light palette (rgb(179, 213, 13), black text); the dark screenshot is byte-identical to the default capture.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark surface and text tokens.

findings.summary: Page and state changes have no View Transition treatment.
findings.evidence: The DOM/CSS probe found no view-transition CSS or startViewTransition usage across the MPA entry surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Add cross-document View Transitions for same-origin navigation, with reduced-motion-safe fallbacks.

findings.summary: Long pages provide no scroll-state-aware navigation or progress feedback.
findings.evidence: The home page is over 2,100 CSS px tall, while CSS inspection found no scroll-state container rules, progress indicator, or animation timeline.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll progress or scroll-state-aware sticky header where it improves orientation.

findings.summary: In-page navigation does not clearly cue the destination or focus change.
findings.evidence: The DOM contains hundreds of hash-only links and no View Transition, highlight, or scroll-marker signal; the crawler screenshot also shows overlapping in-page navigation over content.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real destination links and visible target/focus highlighting for in-page jumps.

findings.summary: A consent interstitial obscures the entire primary experience on every fresh visit.
findings.evidence: Desktop, mobile, detail, listing, and creation screenshots all open behind a modal consent wall for personalised advertising and 210 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the blocking first-load wall with a compact, equally actionable consent surface and keep core content usable.

findings.summary: Consent UI uses custom role dialogs rather than native dialog semantics and has no direct dismiss/decline action.
findings.evidence: The probe found four role=dialog overlays but zero dialog or popover elements; the first layer offers only Consent and Manage options.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native dialog for the modal decision, include an immediate decline/close action, and restore focus on dismissal.

findings.summary: Dense legacy chrome and repeated sidebars crowd the content.
findings.evidence: The desktop/crawler screenshots show multiple stacked navigation strips, boxed regions, sidebars, icon rows, and overlapping in-page navigation competing with the main content.
findings.suggestedFix: Simplify repeated navigation and framing, prioritising the current page’s main content and primary action.

findings.summary: Mobile devices receive a 980px desktop layout scaled down to fit.
findings.evidence: At a requested 360x800 viewport, layout reported no viewport meta and a 980px layout/client width at scale 0.367; text and controls are tiny in the mobile screenshot.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a standard width=device-width viewport and rebuild fixed desktop regions with fluid intrinsic layouts.

findings.summary: Components do not adapt to their available container.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection across the representative page found zero @container rules; the whole desktop composition is merely scaled on mobile.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container queries for reusable cards, rankings, sidebars, and creation-form groups.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly styled and scaled mobile targets are too small.
findings.evidence: Programmatic focus on the first link computed outline: none 0px and no box shadow; the absent viewport meta shrinks controls to 36.7% on mobile.
findings.suggestedFix: Add strong :focus-visible styling and maintain at least 44 CSS px touch targets in a real mobile layout.

findings.summary: The consent wall hides the site purpose and primary actions on arrival.
findings.evidence: Every fresh-load screenshot places the advertising-consent decision above the site’s search, read, and create actions.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the purpose and core actions available while presenting a proportionate privacy choice.

findings.summary: Reading and creation journeys begin with an avoidable consent detour.
findings.evidence: The homepage, sample story, listing, and 329-control creation form are all blocked visually until the visitor opens consent options or accepts.
findings.suggestedFix: Let visitors continue to reading and creation without accepting personalised advertising.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint is well outside the good range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured FCP 4.5s, LCP 5.7s, Speed Index 7.4s, and performance 0.63; the independent trace measured LCP 3.77s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the actual LCP resource and defer consent, ads, analytics, and non-critical scripts.

findings.summary: Legacy synchronous scripts and dependency chains delay rendering.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 94 requests and identified parser-inserted jQuery 1.4.4, jquery-cookie, localStorage, analytics, and other scripts; DOM confirmation shows these scripts are neither async nor defer.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove obsolete dependencies and defer or conditionally load non-critical scripts.

findings.summary: Third-party JavaScript dominates the transfer budget.
findings.evidence: HAR measured 633,623 script bytes; ads (190KB), GTM (158KB), and consent scripts (about 144KB) are the largest resources, with 92 of 94 requests classed third-party.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit third-party value, remove duplicate ad loads, and load optional scripts only after a relevant consent/action.

findings.summary: Core images, links, frames, and creation inputs lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 40 of 44 images without alt. Lighthouse failed image-alt, link-name, and frame-title. The creation form has 179 visible non-button controls without labels.
findings.suggestedFix: Give meaningful images alt text, decorative images empty alt, title frames, name links, and associate every form control with a label.

findings.summary: Text and essential links fail minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s color-contrast audit failed, and its link-in-text-block audit found links relying on color alone.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt contrast-tested color tokens and add non-color link affordances.

findings.summary: Document structure and keyboard focus are not reliable.
findings.evidence: There is no main/nav/header/footer landmark, Lighthouse failed heading order and main-landmark checks, and focused links compute no outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Add semantic landmarks and ordered headings, then provide a visible :focus-visible indicator.

findings.summary: Mobile text is rendered as a miniaturised desktop page.
findings.evidence: At 360px, Chrome lays out 980 CSS px and scales the page to 0.367, making body copy and controls too small to read comfortably.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a real responsive viewport and fluid type/spacing with comfortable line lengths.

findings.summary: The page does not reflow for a narrow viewport.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed meta-viewport; both homepage and detail layout captures remained 980px wide at a requested 360px viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width=device-width and ensure content reflows without relying on whole-page scaling.

findings.summary: Document and image asset hygiene is poor.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported a doctype failure; 38 of 44 images lack dimensions, 43 use legacy formats, and 34 below-fold images are not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a standards-mode HTML5 doctype consistently and add intrinsic dimensions, lazy loading, and modern image formats.

findings.summary: The public site is not mobile-friendly despite crawlable links.
findings.evidence: All four templates lack a viewport meta tag; mobile evidence renders a 980px page at 36.7% scale. Robots.txt is reachable and Lighthouse says anchors are crawlable.
findings.suggestedFix: Add the standard responsive viewport and preserve descriptive real-href links.

findings.summary: Canonical and sitemap signals are incomplete.
findings.evidence: The home probe found no canonical link; /sitemap.xml returns 404. The discoverability fetch also reported an unexpected finalUrl using http although the browser remained on HTTPS.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a canonical HTTPS URL per public template and a sitemap consistent with robots.txt.

findings.summary: Entity pages lack structured data.
findings.evidence: The homepage has Open Graph tags but zero JSON-LD blocks; the sample content page represents a creative work that could expose schema.org metadata.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate WebSite/Organization metadata and CreativeWork or Article JSON-LD on content pages.

findings.summary: HTTPS is undermined by missing security headers and insecure cookies.
findings.evidence: Headers found no CSP, HSTS, or nosniff. All 12 observed cookies lack Secure and use SameSite=None, including several 390–400 day cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Set CSP, HSTS, nosniff, and secure least-privilege cookie attributes; retire obsolete analytics cookies.

findings.summary: The page has an excessive tracking and third-party footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found 11 third-party origins and four known tracker domains; the consent UI names 210 partners and the HAR assigns 859,735 of 879,977 transferred bytes to third parties.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce partners and analytics to the minimum, delay optional requests until consent, and prefer aggregate first-party measurement.

findings.summary: Account and anonymous-edit flows rely on passwords without phishing-resistant authentication.
findings.evidence: The creation flow exposes a password field and current-page probes found no WebAuthn/PublicKeyCredential usage; no permission calls fire on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkeys for accounts and secure recovery; retain contextual permission timing.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: Headers found no clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, CSP/frame-ancestors, HSTS, or nosniff.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP with frame-ancestors plus HSTS, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and nosniff.

findings.summary: The app-like creation service is neither linked as installable nor available offline.
findings.evidence: /manifest.json exists, but the DOM has no manifest link and there is no controlling service worker.
findings.suggestedFix: Link the manifest, provide suitable icons, register a service worker, and offer a lightweight offline fallback.

findings.summary: The consent choice is asymmetric and a direct refusal is hidden.
findings.evidence: The first layer presents a prominent Consent button and Manage options, but no Reject/Decline button, while requesting personalised processing by 210 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Present Accept and Reject with equal prominence and make withdrawal as easy as acceptance.

findings.summary: The creation form lacks robust field semantics for preventing and explaining mistakes.
findings.evidence: The 329-control form has zero required controls and 179 visible unlabelled controls; this prevents dependable native validation and accessible error association.
findings.suggestedFix: Label fields, mark actual requirements, validate after interaction, and announce a concise error summary.

findings.summary: The large creation form provides almost no autocomplete assistance.
findings.evidence: Only one of 267 visible controls has a non-empty autocomplete value; email and password/account-adjacent inputs do not expose appropriate tokens in the captured DOM.
findings.suggestedFix: Add correct autocomplete tokens such as email, current-password/new-password, name, and url where applicable.

findings.summary: Password-based anonymous editing creates avoidable account and recovery risk.
findings.evidence: The create flow asks for email and an editing password while the site offers no passkey signal; users are warned that guessed passwords permit unauthorised editing.
findings.suggestedFix: Move editing ownership into secured accounts, add passkeys and clear recovery/revocation controls.

findings.summary: Most images use legacy formats and lack responsive delivery.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 43 legacy-format images, zero modern-format images, eight missing srcset, and 34 below-fold images without lazy loading.
findings.suggestedFix: Convert photographic/decorative assets to AVIF/WebP, add responsive sources, dimensions, and lazy loading.

findings.summary: Optional advertising and analytics create disproportionate background work.
findings.evidence: HAR records 92 third-party requests and 633KB of scripts for a text/listing page; tracker evidence confirms active analytics and ad domains.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove redundant trackers and gate optional fetches and processing behind explicit consent or interaction.

findings.summary: Third-party resources consume nearly the entire page budget.
findings.evidence: 859,735 of 879,977 transferred bytes are attributed to third-party origins; ads, tag management, consent, and a 48KB font dominate a largely text-based page.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a strict third-party budget, self-host/subset fonts, and defer ads until they can provide user value.

taskList.title: Build a genuine mobile layout and visible keyboard focus
Make consent non-blocking, symmetric, and privacy-minimised
Fix accessible names, labels, landmarks, contrast, and form errors
Reduce LCP and remove/defer legacy and third-party scripts
Deploy defensive headers and secure cookie attributes
Modernise image delivery and enforce a third-party budget
Add canonical, sitemap, and structured metadata
Modernise navigation feedback and page transitions
Add install/offline support for the creation experience
